\mxunit{enrichment-invariants-notes}{Parity and invariants}
\mxsubtitle{High school · reasoning \textperiodcentered{} Lesson and method \textperiodcentered{} 01}

\begin{prerequisites}
Even and odd integers; proof by contradiction.
\end{prerequisites}

\begin{keypoint}[Ideas and method]
An invariant is a quantity or property preserved by every allowed move. If the target has a different invariant value from the initial state, it cannot be reached.

To study parity, replace integers with their remainders 0 or 1 modulo 2. Two odd integers have an even sum. Adding an even integer preserves parity.

Method: specify one move, find what it preserves, and compute the invariant at the start and at the target. An obstruction proves impossibility; the absence of an obstruction does not prove possibility.
\end{keypoint}

\begin{example}
Start at 0 and add or subtract 6 at each move. Every reachable number is even, so 15 is unreachable. The number 14 is also unreachable, but parity alone cannot prove this: every reachable number is a multiple of 6.
\end{example}

\begin{activity}[Explore]
Write several sequences of moves, then classify the reached numbers. Find a common property more precise than parity.
\end{activity}
